[[Category:Cognitive bias]]
'''Cognitive dissonance''' describes the state that an individual's belief and behaviour are contradictory.

== Psychological discomfort ==

Self-report study [[Source:On the motivational nature of cognitive dissonance: Dissonance as psychological discomfort (Scholarly article)|name-author]] finds cognitive dissonance a source of discomfort<ref>{{#cite:Q3625}}</ref>, which [[Source:Twenty years of cognitive dissonance: Case study of the evolution of a theory (Scholarly article)|name-author]] hypothesises is caused by the contradiction's threat to one's [[self-image]].<ref>{{#cite:Q3620}}</ref>

== Reconciliation ==

[[File:Cognitive dissonance.png|thumbnail|To alleviate '''psychological discomfort''' from '''cognitive dissonance''', a smoker may stops smoking, or simply deny the adverse effects of smoking on their health.]]
To alleviate psychological discomfort, individuals spontaneously seek to resolve the cognitive dissonance, either by

* adapting their behaviour;
* or convincing themselves of a new belief more coherent with their behaviour

<ref>{{#cite:Q3470}}</ref>
